strongest_angle: The collapse of the 90-foot Hōlei Sea Arch in Hawaiʻi Volcanoes National Park illustrates the inevitable geological lifecycle of coastal landmarks formed by volcanic activity and persistent ocean erosion.

key_facts.fact: The Hōlei Sea Arch in Hawaiʻi Volcanoes National Park stood 90 feet (27.4 meters) tall before its collapse into the Pacific Ocean.
National Park Service records confirm the arch was last seen intact on September 23, 2026, and was confirmed gone by the night of September 27, 2026.
The Hōlei Sea Arch was located at the end of Chain of Craters Road on the southern coastline of the island of Hawaiʻi.
The Guardian reported that the collapse followed a series of rough storms in the region during the weeks leading up to the event.
